newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power slips on milder weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power slips on milder weather.

text.p: Forecast of temperatures moderating from recent lows next week pressured spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. on Friday
"The warmer weather is forcast to come, and that's what we're looking at," said a New York trader.

For Saturday, the Northeast was predicted to hit peak temperatures in the 30s-40s Fahrenheit and off-peak temperatures in the teens. Sub-zero degree temperatures were forecast at the Vermont-New Hampshire border during Saturday's evening and early morning hours.
Extended outlook indicated weather in the northeastern corner of the country would be slightly warmer-than-normal.

In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Saturday delivery was quoted at $18.00-$19.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), for Sunday $17.00-$17.50 and for Monday near $24.00. Today quotes compared with Thursday's $23.00-$25.00 for Friday.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Monday was assessed near $14.00, down from a quote of $15.00 on Thursday.

In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Saturday was valued near $20.00, for Sunday near $19.00 and for Monday at $27.00-$29.00, lower than Thursday's $31.00-$32.00 for Friday delivery.
Off-peak, non-firm Monday electricity in eastern NYPP was notationally assessed at $15.00-$18.00, compared with a range of $17.00-$18.50 on Thursday.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday at the Northeast Utilities border was notationally pegged at $35.00-$36.00, down from Thursday's $36.00-$37.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Monday delivery to the NU border traded near $20.00, the lower end of Thursday's range.
NEPOOL spot business was very thin today. "The (bid/ask) margin was too wide," a NEPOOL market source said.
Separately, the 619 megawatt (MW) oil-fired Wyman 4 generating unit in Yarmouth, Maine, was expected to resume operation Tuesday after being shut October 5 for seasonal maintenance.
Swing natural gas prices this weekend at the New York City gate were assessed at $3.30-$3.40 per million British thermal units, compared with Thursday's $3.70-$3.80 for Friday.
"If it stays warm, prices will really come down," said the New York trader.
